title: FR-008: Event builder with origin tagging
body:
**Requirement (P0).** Event builder with origin tagging. Emits `enter`, `exit`, `cross`, `touch` (person mask overlaps a protected object), `removed` (watched object disappears while a person overlaps it) and `dwell`. When more than one person mask overlaps a protected or watched object, one `touch` (or `removed`) event is emitted per overlapping track, each carrying its own subject's `actor_role`; rules are evaluated per event. Each event has an ID, camera, times, track, clip range and the `actor_role` of its subject (filled in after visit assembly, FR-044). Each track also gets an `origin_zone`: the zone, by `kind` (`egress`, `perimeter`, `interior_yard`), that contains the track's foot point in the majority of its first 10 frames (1 s); no zone or a tie gives `null`. The origin is `null` unless that camera observed without interruption for the 2 s before the track's first frame: no outage, no skipped or unprocessed window, and not the first frame of a window whose predecessor was skipped. An `egress` origin is also `null` when any person track on that camera that did not itself originate in that egress zone was last seen overlapping the egress polygon, dilated by 50%, within the preceding 10 min

**Depends on:** FR-007, FR-019

**Acceptance criteria:** Synthetic-track unit tests pass for every event type. A track born inside `front_door_egress` gets that origin; a track born mid-yard gets `null`; a track re-born in `front_door_egress` 5 s after a courier's track ended there gets `null`; a track whose first frame follows a skipped window gets `null`. Two overlapping tracks on `po_side_gate` give two touch events. Each demo scenario yields its labelled events and origins

**Blocked by:** nothing (offline-buildable)

title: FR-010: Visit assembly
body:
**Requirement (P0).** Visit assembly. Tracks are linked across cameras only when the gap fits a topology edge and the notes agree; two or more candidates means no link. *(Unchanged, plus:)* the visit records one subject chain per linked set of tracks, which carries the role (FR-044). When a link on a non-blind edge is ambiguous only because 2 or more candidates entered the edge together, every candidate holds the same role, and the same number of tracks emerge, each emerging chain takes that role with basis `group:<role>` while the tracks stay unlinked. This never applies across a blind-spot edge

**Depends on:** FR-008, FR-009

**Acceptance criteria:** Link precision at least 90% on the labelled set

**Blocked by:** hardware

title: FR-021: Typed rules
body:
**Requirement (P0).** Typed rules. Spark compiles text into rule JSON whose targets are limited to existing objects and zones. Identity phrases map to roles, never to people: "anyone except family", "except us" and "not the household" → `non_household`; "strangers only" and "not guests or deliveries" → `external_visitor_only`; a named person ("except Sam") → `non_household` plus the notice "Vigil can't recognise individuals. It treats someone as household only if they came out of the house's own doors or checked in on the app, so Sam is exempt only in those cases." The draft card states the basis: *"Vigil treats someone as household only when it saw them come out of the house's own doors, or when a household member checked in on the app just before coming into view. Household members arriving from the street without checking in, and anyone Vigil loses track of, count as non-household and can trigger this rule. Vigil places people by where they came from; it does not identify anyone and creates no face, voice or body templates."* The owner confirms

**Depends on:** FR-012, FR-019, FR-044

**Acceptance criteria:** At least 9 of 10 reference phrasings compile to the expected JSON, including 3 role phrasings. An unresolvable target asks a question. No compiled rule ever names a person

**Blocked by:** credits

title: FR-029: Expected Guest / Delivery Window and owner check-in (was "owner label")
body:
**Requirement (P1).** Expected Guest / Delivery Window and owner check-in (was "owner label"). The owner sets a time window before it starts (start and end, optional cameras or zones, optional label such as "plumber" or "deliveries"). Subjects whose first track starts in a `perimeter` zone in the window's scope while it is active are `expected_visitor` (FR-044 step 3). Windows are capped at 12 h, show on the cards, and can be cancelled. The post-hoc "This was expected" button stays as feedback only and never changes a verdict retroactively. Also: an "I'm outside" check-in (LAN app, `POST /api/checkin`), single-use and never retroactive, which binds at most one subject chain in the 120 s after the tap (FR-044 step 2); an unused check-in expires after 30 min

**Depends on:** FR-044

**Acceptance criteria:** A subject arriving inside an active window is `expected_visitor`, and one arriving from a perimeter zone 1 s after it ends, or on a camera outside its scope, is `external_visitor`; one with a `null` origin is `unknown`. Windows persist and expire. A check-in binds at most one chain

**Blocked by:** nothing (offline-buildable)

**Depends on:** FR-035, FR-036, FR-019

**Acceptance criteria:** Mean reprojection on the 6 landmarks under 6 px at 1280 px (nominal FOV) or under 4 px (lens profile). The audit-harness held-out ground error is reported per camera, target under 0.25 m

title: FR-044: Spatial origin roles (new; no identification)
body:
**Requirement (P0).** Spatial origin roles (new; no identification). `visits.py` assigns each subject chain an `actor_role` from evidence only, in this order: (1) its first track's `origin_zone` is an `egress` zone of the house → `household_insider`, basis `egress:<zone>`; (2) an explicit check-in binds it: a household member tapped "I'm outside" in the LAN app (passive Wi-Fi presence never counts). A check-in is single-use and never retroactive. When the 120 s interval after the tap closes, it binds the one subject chain whose first track started in that interval with `origin_zone` `null`, `interior_yard` or `perimeter` (never `egress`), but only if exactly one such chain started and no subject other than `household_insider` was in view on any camera at that chain's first frame; otherwise it binds nothing. A bound chain is `household_insider` with basis `checkin:<id>`. An unused check-in expires after 30 min; (3) its first track's `origin_zone` is a `perimeter` zone on a camera (or zone) in the scope of an Expected Window (FR-029) that is active at that track's first frame → `expected_visitor`, basis `window:<id>`. A window with no listed cameras or zones covers every perimeter zone. A `null` origin never becomes `expected_visitor`; (4) its origin is a `perimeter` zone → `external_visitor`, basis `perimeter:<zone>`; (5) otherwise → `unknown`, basis `ambiguous_link:<track_id>` when its first track followed an ambiguous link, else `origin_null:<track_id>` (origin `null` or an `interior_yard` zone); the same-role group rule in FR-010 (basis `group:<role>`) is the only exception. Roles carry across a link only when the link is unambiguous. Across a blind-spot gap, `external_visitor` carries on any unambiguous re-link (it can only make rules fire). `household_insider` and `expected_visitor` carry only when both tracks' appearance notes agree on at least one attribute that is not `unknown` (upper colour, lower colour or a carried item). A re-link on transit time alone, as at night under IR, makes the chain `unknown` with basis `gap_unresolved:<gap_id>`. Every role has a stored `role_basis` shown in the trace. If FR-029 is not built, step (3) never matches and FR-044 still passes

**Depends on:** FR-008, FR-010 (FR-029 and the check-in only supply inputs; without them, rules (2) and (3) never apply)

**Acceptance criteria:** Truth table over origin × check-in × window × link outcome. Scenario A subject = `household_insider` (basis `egress:front_door_egress`); scenario C subject = `external_visitor` (basis `perimeter:side_alley`). An ambiguous re-link gives `unknown`. A household subject enters `shed_back`; a never-seen person with `unknown` colours emerges inside 5–180 s → `unknown`. Two household members leave the front door together and two tracks emerge on `side_left` → both `household_insider` (basis `group:household_insider`). Two chains starting in one check-in's 120 s interval → neither is bound. No face, voice, body or name field exists in any person-related schema (NFR-003). EVAL reports assigned vs labelled role per subject, day and night separately, including the share of household subjects not assigned `household_insider` (role miss rate) and the alerts it caused

**Blocked by:** hardware
